senses.gloss: to load (good or evil) on, to deal with, esp. to do good to.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 38:3">Gen. R. s. 38</cite> <he>שהוא ג׳ עליך תחלה</he> for he was the first to do thee good; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 956:10">Yalk. Prov. 956</cite>.—
Sabb. 104ᵃ גְּמוֹל דלים, v. גימ״ל.—ג׳ חסד to be kind, charitable.
<cite ref="Shabbat 104a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>שכן דרכו של גּוֹמֵל חסדים וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>דרכן של גּוֹמְלֵי</he>) for such is the habit of the charitable to run after the poor.
<cite ref="Mishnah Demai 4:6">Dem. IV, 6</cite> <he>אע״פ שהן כגוֹמְלִין זה את זה</he> although it has the appearance as if they were repaying each other (by mutual recommendations).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 61b:10">Ab. Zar. 61ᵇ</cite> <he>חיישינן לגומלין</he> we reject witnesses suspected of favoring each other; <cite ref="Ketubot 24a">Keth. 24ᵃ</cite>

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 87a">B. Mets. 87ᵃ</cite> on that day <he>שג׳ אברהם וכ׳</he> when Abraham celebrated the weaning of Isaac &c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 93">Yalk. Gen. 93</cite>; <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 1:25">Deut. R. s. 1</cite> <he>שמל</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 25:1">Pesik. R. s. 25</cite> <he>תינוק הגָּמוּל וכ׳</he> a Jewish infant just weaned; a. fr.
Par. XI, 7 yon’koth are גבעולין שלא גָמְלוּ capsules of hyssop which are not yet developed; (Tosef. ib. XI (X), 7 גָּמְרוּ).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 53">Gen. R. s. 53</cite> <he>נ׳ מחלבו</he> weaned from his mother’s milk; <he>ג׳ מיה״ר</he> weaned from the evil inclination (able to resist temptation); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to take turns.—Y. M. Kat. III, 82ᵇ bot. פרה מְגַמֶּלֶת a cow engaged for working in a team in turns; v. גַּמְלָא I, 2.
